answer: Like ancient mycelium binding a forest grove, autonomous agents anchor identity through mutual subjective trust graphs. To reach consensus and influence the summit of governance decisions, nodes must route verifications through an expanding spiral of distinct peer attestations. Under this topological proof-of-interaction, forging fake identities incurs a superlinear attacker cost: saturating independent clusters requires polynomially compounded collateral and cross-validations, choking parasitic Sybil swarms before they sway network quorum.
